title: Strength of Acids & Bases
page_title: Strength of Acids & Bases | Cambridge (CIE) AS Chemistry Revision Notes 2023

blocks.md:
- Strong and weak acids can be distinguished from each other by their:

  - **pH value** (using a pH meter or universal indicator)
  - **Electrical conductivity**
  - **Reactivity**
- An acid **dissociates** into H<sup>+</sup> in solution according to:
- The **stronger** the acid, the **greater** the **concentration of H**<sup>**+**</sup> and therefore the **lower** **the** **pH**

blocks.text: pH values of a strong & weak acids

blocks.md:
- pH of 0.1 mol dm<sup>-3</sup> solution:

  - HCl (strong); pH 1
  - CH<sub>3</sub>COOH (weak); pH about 3

- The most **accurate** way to determine the pH is by reading it off a **pH meter**
- The pH meter is connected to the **pH electrode** which shows the pH value of the solution

blocks.alt: Diagram showing a pH electrode in a solution with a pH meter reading 1.0, indicating acidity; hydrogen ions are illustrated in the solution.
blocks.caption: The diagram shows a digital pH meter measures the pH of a solution using a pH electrode

blocks.md:
- A less accurate method is to measure the pH using universal indicator paper
- The universal indicator paper is dipped into a solution of acid, upon which the paper changes colour
- The colour is then compared to those on a chart which shows the colours corresponding to different pH values

blocks.text: How to use universal indicator paper

blocks.alt: Universal indicator chart showing pH range with colours. Acidic solutions turn indicator orange (pH 1-2) in HCl, yellow (pH 3-4) in CH3COOH.
blocks.caption: The diagram shows the change in colour of the universal indicator paper when dipped in a strong and weak acid. The colour chart is used to read off the corresponding pH values which are between 1-2 for a strong acid and 3-4 for a weak acid

blocks.md:
- Since a **stronger acid **has a **higher concentration of H**<sup>**+**</sup>** **it **conducts electricity **better
- Stronger acids therefore have a greater **electrical conductivity**
- The electrical conductivity can be determined by using a **conductivity meter**
- Like the pH meter, the conductivity meter is connected to an electrode
- The conductivity of the solution can be read off the meter

blocks.alt: Diagram of a conductivity meter displaying 215, showing an electrode in a blue solution. Labels identify the meter, electrode, and solution.
blocks.caption: The diagram shows a digital conductivity meter that measures the electrical conductivity of a solution using an electrode

blocks.md:
- Strong and weak acids of the same concentrations react differently with reactive metals
- This is because the concentration of H<sup>+</sup> is greater in strong acids compared to weak acids
- The greater H<sup>+</sup> concentration means that H<sub>2</sub> gas is produced faster (equal amounts of acid give the same total volume of H<sub>2</sub> when the magnesium is in excess)

blocks.text: The reaction of 0.1 mol dm<sup>-3</sup> of a strong acid, HCl, with Mg

blocks.alt: Diagram of magnesium reacting with hydrochloric acid, producing magnesium chloride and hydrogen gas, shown as bubbles in the solution.
blocks.caption: The reaction produces a lot of bubbles and hydrogen gas due to the high concentration of H+ present in the solution

blocks.text: The reaction of 0.1 mol dm<sup>-3</sup> of a weak acid, CH<sub>3</sub>COOH, with Mg

blocks.alt: Magnesium added to 0.1 mol dm-3 ethanoic acid: magnesium ethanoate forms and a few bubbles of hydrogen are given off.
blocks.caption: The reaction produces fewer bubbles and hydrogen gas due to the lower concentration of H+ present in the solution

blocks.label: Exam Hint
blocks.md:
- The above-mentioned properties of strong and weak acids depend on their ability to dissociate and form H<sup>+</sup> ions.
- Stronger acids dissociate more, producing a greater concentration of H<sup>+</sup> ions and therefore showing lower pH values, greater electrical conductivity and more vigorous reactions with reactive metals.
- A neutralisation reaction is one in which an acid (pH <7) and a base/alkali (pH >7) react together to form water (pH = 7) and a salt:
- The proton of the acid reacts with the hydroxide of the base to form water:

- The spectator ions which are not involved in the formation of water are Na<sup>+</sup> (aq) + Cl<sup>–</sup> (aq)

  - These react to form the salt:
- The name of the salt produced can be predicted from the acid that has reacted

- Hydrochloric acid forms **chloride **salts
- Sulfuric acid forms **sulfate** salts
- Nitric acid forms **nitrate** salts
- Ethanoic acid forms **ethanoate** salts

blocks.label: Exam Hint
blocks.md:
Note that the reaction of an acid and metal carbonate also forms carbon dioxide:

**acid + metal carbonate → salt + water + carbon dioxide**
